question_record.context: A suspicious remote activity on a machine occurred as part of a recent security incident. This incident involved attempts to initiate interactive sessions, modify files, pass WMI commands, create scheduled tasks, and other potentially malicious activities from a remote machine. Notably, the file `cmd.exe` was executed with ProcessId `8896` on 2024-07-02, indicating a possibility of a remote activity. The compromised machine is yet to be identified (host name missing).
question_record.question: What account was responsible for the launching of the renamed and executed system executable in the end alert?
solution: Suspicious remote activity was observed on the host `mb-adfs` which could involve actions such as initiating interactive sessions, modifying files, passing WMI commands, or creating scheduled tasks.
A system executable that was renamed was launched on the account `SYSTEM`, indicating possible attempts to use it for malicious activities or to connect to an attacker-controlled network.

37.name: Suspicious remote activity
37.description: Suspicious activity initiated remotely was observed on this machine. This alert can flag attempts to initiate interactive sessions, modify files, pass WMI commands, create scheduled tasks, and other potentially malicious activities from a remote machine.

27.name: System executable renamed and launched
27.description: A Windows executable file that has been renamed was launched. Attackers might be attempting to use the executable to perform malicious activities, such as running malicious code or connecting to an attacker-controlled network address. By changing the path or file name of a system executable, attackers can avoid certain behavior-based detection technologies that rely on default paths and file names.

interpretation.scope: official graph witness, not a proof of causality, actor identity or autonomous planning
